q1_issues.issue: The comparative "older" is asserted as the positive property (Member sk_plant_1 old), which a comparative does not entail, and it is predicated of the group symbol instead of distributing to its members.
The definite "the efficiency" is typed only inside the sealed Theme term, but a definite referent inside a seal must project its typing atom to top level.
Both comparatives that carry the sentence's point — "more power" and "more cheaply" — are dropped without trace.
The parenthetical appositive "the most affected segment" is the writer's own assertion, not part of what is hoped, yet it is sealed inside the hope complement.

q2_gaps: an attitude NOUN with a that-clause complement in a specificational copular clause ("The administration's hope is that P") — the attitude section covers only attitude VERBS, and the genitive rule would give (Possession hope administration) rather than the Experiencer used here
a bare attributive comparative with no stated standard ("older plants", "more power", "more cheaply") — Comparatives & degree always requires an explicit "than Y", so these are unrepresentable

a bare plural in an argument / oblique-object position ("the efficiency of older coal-fired plants") — the determiner rule makes a bare plural generic, and the oblique-object rule lists only articles, mass nouns, domains and proper names
whether definitional decomposition atoms (a fused compound's genus) belong inside or outside a seal
notes: The complement is correctly sealed under a non-factive attitude with no top-level predication, and the (Most affected sk_plant_1 segment) superlative is well-formed with its class atom. Whether "the administration's hope" should take Experiencer, as here, or the genitive's Possession is the first coverage question above.
